research.label: Dogs Trust: enrichment ideas for bored dogs

substitutes: No pen? Use your phone's notes.
variations: Short version: one bench within a block or two of home.
Seated version: a bench within thirty feet of a parking spot or accessible entry.
Slow version: stay twenty minutes and rate only the smells.
Yard version: rate the spots in your own yard or balcony.
title: The Scenic Bench Club
clue: A seat you have never tried is waiting, and it may be the best one in town.
reveal: Hunt for a new bench with a view and give it a proper audition. Each bench gets a short name and three honest ratings: view, shade and smells. Over time you build a collection of favorite seats.
objective: Find a new bench, sit there with your dog, and give it a name and a three-part rating card.
instructions: Pick a neighborhood or park you do not usually use, and look for a bench with a view. Check it is on a public path where dogs are allowed on leash.
Walk there at an easy pace and let your dog sniff on the way. Bring water and a mat in case the ground is more comfortable than the seat.
Audition the bench: sit for at least ten minutes. Watch what your dog does; many settle, watch passers-by or quietly sniff the air.

Rate it out of five for each of three things: View (what you can see), Shade (how comfortable in the sun and wind) and Smells (how interested your dog is). Never ask your dog to stay put for the rating.
Give the bench a name that reflects what happened, such as 'The Duck Pond Seat' or 'Squirrel Corner'.
Write the name and ratings on a card or in your phone notes. Take a photo of the bench from a short distance.
Head home, or try a second bench on the way if your dog is still happy.
twist: Every bench gets a name and a three-part rating, so your outings build a collection of favorite seats.
completion: Counts once you have sat on a new bench with your dog and written its name and rating.
photoIdea: The bench with your dog beside it, or a view from the bench with your dog's tail or ears in the frame.
memoryPrompt: Which bench did you find, and what did your dog make of it?
supplies: Paper and a pen or a phone

reservation.note: Check local leash and dog rules; use public benches only.

safety: Check the ground and bench are comfortable in the sun, and offer water; leave if your dog is too warm or cold.
Keep your dog leashed and clear of other walkers on narrow paths.
Stay near traffic-free paths and never tie your dog to a bench and walk away.
teaser: Every neighborhood hides a perfect seat, and your dog may already know where it is.
